# Funding rate mechanics and mark price — facts

## How it works

- [statement] Velocity funding is lazy: it updates when a position is opened or closed and again once enough time has passed, with one-hour periods (an update in the first 20 minutes rounds back onto the hour). A market that neither trades nor gets cranked does not advance its cumulative rates; owed funding shows as unrealized P&L and settles at the account's next action in that market. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/trading/funding-rates · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price
- [statement] Hyperliquid's mark price is the median of three inputs: (1) oracle price plus a 150-second EMA of the gap between Hyperliquid's mid and the oracle; (2) the median of Hyperliquid's best bid, best ask and last trade; (3) the median of perp mid prices from Binance, OKX, Bybit, Gate IO and MEXC. The oracle is a weighted median of CEX spot prices updated by validators about every 3 seconds (CEX weights Binance 3, OKX 2, Bybit 2, Gate IO 1, MEXC 1). Mark is used for margining, liquidation, TP/SL triggers and unrealized PnL. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/robust-price-indices · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price · also: https://hyperliquid-co.gitbook.io/community-docs/introduction/roadmap/2025-26-03_incident
- [statement] Academic work treats funding as the mechanism that substitutes for expiry convergence: because perpetuals never mature, longs pay shorts a rate tied to the perp-spot gap. He et al. derive no-arbitrage prices and find crypto perp deviations larger than in traditional FX, shrinking over time. Kim and Park propose path-dependent funding rates as a practical alternative. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.06888 · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.08573v1
- [statement] Hyperliquid's mark price is the median of three inputs: (1) the oracle price plus a 150-second EMA of (Hyperliquid mid - oracle); (2) the median of Hyperliquid's best bid, best ask and last trade; (3) the median of Binance, OKX, Bybit, Gate IO and MEXC perp mid prices with weights 3, 2, 2, 1, 1. If exactly two of the three inputs exist, a 30-second EMA of input (2) is added. Mark price drives margining, liquidations, TP/SL triggers and unrealized PnL. The oracle price, a weighted median of CEX spot prices that validators update about every 3 seconds, drives funding. The mark-price page is marked 'Last updated 1 year ago'. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/robust-price-indices · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price · also: https://hyperliquid-co.gitbook.io/community-docs/introduction/roadmap/2025-26-03_incident
- [statement] On Velocity, update_funding_rate runs only when the market's funding period has elapsed on the hour grid. If the previous update landed more than one third of a period (20 minutes for a one-hour period) after the hour, the next update waits until the following period. The program skips the update if funding is paused, the oracle is invalid, or the mark and oracle prices diverge too far. Funding accrues into per-market cumulative long and short rates. Each account settles the difference on its next action in that market (trade, deposit, withdrawal or explicit settle). Until then the amount shows as unrealized P&L, and a market that nobody trades or cranks does not advance its rates. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/velocity-exchange/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/controller/funding.rs · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price · also: https://github.com/velocity-exchange/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/math/helpers.rs, https://docs.velocity.exchange/trading/funding-rates
- [statement] Drift's funding update is permissionless and lazy. The `update_funding_rate` instruction has no signer in its account list and only applies when `on_the_hour_update` returns zero; an update that lands later than one third of the period (20 minutes) past the hour pushes the next update a full period later. Payments are credited separately: each account settles against per-side cumulative rates on its next action, and `SettleFundingPayment` is permissionless (Neodyme). Velocity's docs describe the same lazy hourly cadence, and a market that neither trades nor gets cranked does not advance its cumulative rates. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/instructions/keeper.rs · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price · also: https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/math/helpers.rs, https://neodyme.io/reports/Drift.pdf, https://docs.velocity.exchange/trading/funding-rates

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Velocity caps the funding premium at 3% of oracle TWAP for contract tiers A and B, 5% for tier C and 10% below C. The AMM acts as counterparty to imbalance and may spend at most one third of its retained equity per funding period; the insurance fund is not used to cover funding shortfalls. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/trading/funding-rates · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price
- [statement] Perpetuals never expire, so nothing forces convergence to spot. Exchanges have longs pay shorts a funding rate tied to the perp-spot gap, typically every 8 hours and approximately the average gap over the prior 8 hours. He, Manela, Ross and von Wachter derive no-arbitrage perpetual prices in which the funding 'clamp' matters (a small fixed rate when prices are close, linear in the gap beyond). They find mean absolute deviations of about 52% to 90% a year in crypto, larger than in traditional currency markets, declining about 22 percentage points a year. Kim and Park model funding as an average over the past 8 hours and show the perpetual price stays uniquely determined and close to the instantaneous-spot version. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.06888 · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.08573v1

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Jupiter's GUM-engine beta markets (JUP, HYPE, ZEC and stock perps) charge hourly funding instead of a borrow fee. Funding accrues while a position is open and is applied every hour on the hour (UTC); a positive rate means longs pay shorts. The mark price is an oracle price (Chainlink for the stock markets) used for margin, PnL and liquidation, and a beta position is liquidated when the mark price reaches its liquidation price. The docs publish no funding formula, cap or reference price for these markets. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/beta-markets · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price · also: https://solanacompass.com/news/jupiter-perps-adds-six-markets-including-tokenized-spacex-hype-and-zec-via-gum-orderbook

## Facts and statements

- [statement] On Hyperliquid, premium = impact_price_difference / oracle_price, where impact_price_difference = max(impact_bid_px - oracle_px, 0) - max(oracle_px - impact_ask_px, 0). HIP-3 perps use a more responsive premium, (0.5 * (impact_bid_px + impact_ask_px) / oracle_px) - 1. The funding payment is position_size * oracle_price * funding_rate: the spot oracle price, not the mark price, converts size to notional. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/funding · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price
- [statement] Jupiter Perps' newer beta markets run on the GUM orderbook engine and do charge funding: it accrues while a position is open and is applied every hour on the hour (UTC), positive rate meaning longs pay shorts. The beta-markets page publishes no formula, no cap, and does not say which price funding uses; mark price there is an oracle price (Chainlink for stock markets). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/beta-markets · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/fees, https://solanacompass.com/news/jupiter-perps-adds-six-markets-including-tokenized-spacex-hype-and-zec-via-gum-orderbook
- [statement] Velocity aims to charge longs and shorts the same rate. The AMM takes the other side of any long/short imbalance and pays from its own retained equity: at most one third of its fee pool per funding period. If the cost would exceed that, the receiving side's rate is capped, so the cumulative long and short funding rates diverge. If the AMM is the net receiver, it keeps the difference as revenue. The insurance fund is never drawn on to cover a funding shortfall. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/velocity-exchange/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/math/funding.rs · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price · also: https://docs.velocity.exchange/trading/funding-rates
- [statement] Each successful Drift funding update emits a `FundingRateRecord` with funding_rate, funding_rate_long, funding_rate_short, both cumulative rates, mark_price_twap, oracle_price_twap and period_revenue, and each user settlement emits a `FundingPaymentRecord`. These events are the on-chain audit trail for what was charged and from which TWAP inputs. (low confidence) — https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/controller/funding.rs · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price
- [statement] At the time of JELLY, a community wiki lists the perp-mid input to Hyperliquid's mark price as Binance, OKX and Bybit only, and notes Bybit's weight of 2 in the oracle; the current official docs list five venues for that input (adding Gate IO and MEXC). The sources do not say whether the change followed the incident. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid-co.gitbook.io/community-docs/introduction/roadmap/2025-26-03_incident · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/robust-price-indices
- [statement] Hyperliquid's Info API exposes funding, markPx, oraclePx and premium per asset through metaAndAssetCtxs, and fundingHistory returns one record per hour with the rate actually charged. fundingHistory does not return the oracle price, so estimating past payments needs a separate oracle or mark series. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-11) — https://www.dwellir.com/guides/hyperliquid-funding-rates · keywords: Funding rate mechanics and mark price
